  "concordance_definition": "A replication is considered successful if it succeeds on a majority of five criteria (i.e., three or more). The five criteria were: (i) direction and statistical significance (p < 0.05); (ii) original effect size in replication 95% confidence interval; (iii) replication effect size in original 95% confidence interval; (iv) replication effect size in original 95% prediction interval; (v) meta-analysis combining original and replication effect sizes is statistically significant (p < 0.05).",

    "The selection process for papers and experiments might have introduced bias.",
    "Replications were conducted on a subset of experiments from the papers, and it's possible less replicable experiments were inadvertently selected.",
    "The generalizability of findings is unclear due to selection and replication process.",
    "The possibility of methodological error in the replications cannot be ruled out.",
    "Differences in experimental contexts (samples, reagents, instruments, climate, software, time of year, physical environment) between original and replication experiments, even if deemed irrelevant a priori, could be critical.",

    "50 of the 193 experiments (26%) planned to be repeated were completed.",
    "158 effects could be compared with the same effects in the original paper.",
    "136 of the 158 effects (86%) reported in the original papers were positive effects.",
    "22 (14%) of the effects were null effects.",
    "117 (74%) of the effects were supported by a numerical result.",
    "41 (26%) were supported by a representative image.",
    "For original positive effects, 43% of replication effects were statistically significant and in the same direction as the original effect.",
    "For original null effects, 73% replication effects were null results.",
    "17 of the 97 (18%) original positive effect sizes were in the 95% confidence interval of the replication effect size.",

    "For original positive effects, 58% (95% CI: [44%, 72%]) could be considered successful according to the prediction interval criterion.",

    "For original positive effects, 42% (95% CI: [28%, 56%]) had p orig < 0.05.",

    "92% of replication effect sizes were smaller than the original (combining numeric and representative images).",
    "Original null results were twice as likely as original positive results to mostly replicate successfully (80% vs. 40%) across five dichotomous criteria.",

    "12% of replication effects were in the same direction as the original and statistically significant for animal experiments, compared with 54% for non-animal experiments.",
    "44% of replication effects were in the 95% prediction interval for animal experiments, compared with 63% for non-animal experiments.",
    "For original positive effects, 13% (n=97) replications succeeded on all five criteria.",
    "For original null effects, 47% (n=15) replications succeeded on all five criteria.",
    "Combining positive and null effects, 46% of replications succeeded on more criteria than they failed.",
    "Median effect sizes were 84% smaller than the original findings for animal replications.",
    "Median effect sizes were 78% smaller than the original findings for non-animal replications.",
